title: Calixtus quoted: believing is supernatural; some prior acts are in man's power
source_text: X. Credere, inquit, actio est suo genere supernaturalis, sive sua natura supra vires humanas, propterea Spiritui Sancto eam ascribimus, quod is animum humanum ad credendum excitet, efficiatque ut homo credat, diligat, Deum timeat, imo ut credere, timere & diligere velit, atque sic actus supernaturales, veramque conversionem ingredientes, sive constituentes Deo tribuimus, & in manu hominum positos negamus: ita tamen ut non negemus esse quosdam in hominis potestate sitos, quos ab ipso Deus praestari velit, priusquam ad auxilia & dona supernaturalia progressus fiat, certe quoad modum ordinarium.
pass_a_gloss: X. To believe, he says, is an action supernatural in its kind, or by its nature above human strength, therefore we ascribe it to the Holy Spirit, because he excites the human mind to believe, and brings it about that man believes, loves, fears God, indeed that he wills to believe, to fear & to love, and thus supernatural acts, & those entering into, or constituting true conversion we attribute to God, & deny them placed in men's hand: yet so that we do not deny that there are some placed in man's power, which God wills to be performed by him, before progress is made to supernatural aids & gifts, certainly as regards the ordinary manner.
pass_b_english: Thesis X. 'Believing,' he writes, 'is an action supernatural in kind, that is, beyond human strength by its nature. We credit it to the Holy Spirit because he rouses the human mind to believe and brings it about that a person believes, loves and fears God, and indeed wants to believe, fear and love.

So we assign to God the supernatural acts that enter into, or make up, true conversion, and we deny that they lie in human hands. We do not deny, however, that some acts lie within a person's power, which God wants him to perform before any advance is made to supernatural aids and gifts, at any rate in the ordinary course.'

choices.why: The Roman school's division of grace, kept in its technical terms throughout the locus.

bible_refs: Georg Calixtus, Epitome theologiae (taken down from his dictation), treatise on the ministry of the word, p. 241 (as cited in the print).
